items.title: Lawrence Douglas Harris Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: The interviewee (Lawrence Douglas Harris) never mentions Al Freeman. The mention of Al Freeman occurs entirely within the [INTERVIEWER]'s turn.

ctx.x: They didn't read much. They didn't read.

In fact I don't remember too many of them that I played with until I got my band and Al Freeman really read music he could even transpose to that site. And he saved me but I know of so many piano players that wouldn't even attempt to look at a sheet of music. But they could still play like L.D. says in every key, play everything, no missing note. Well Eddie Hayward's daddy, I knew him personally. I sat in a pit with him in Atlanta, Georgia. He was another great piano player that could conceive an idea in his head…

Talking about sheets though, we're getting away from Lazy Daddy but the guy, the most terrific guy I could, I don't know where I could do anything with sheets, taking my sheet out of my mind, I thought about writing music when he said sheet, was Lester Young's father, old man Billy Young. I played in his band. And you know just like we're sitting here talking, he keeps the conversation going and writing the parts. He said, you didn't write a cue sheet, just sit down and write the part. He might write the cue…
